results.title: 'Humanitarian mission' for Kostiantynivka: Is it a trap?
results.content: Russian President Putin has proposed an evacuation of the Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka, like the recent operation in Oleshky. Experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

results.title: Iraq's risky standoff: The state vs. Iran-allied militias
results.content: This week, Iraqi security forces surrounded an area run by the Kataib Hezbollah militia. Onlookers describe it as the most dangerous confrontation between the Iraqi state and Iran-allied militias in decades.

results.title: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have held trilateral talks ― but what did they achieve?
results.content: The presidents of China, the US and Russia have held an unprecedented summit. While Trump said the three leaders were "making history," Xi described the talks as "fruitful" and Putin called them "open and candid."

results.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
results.content: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

results.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
results.content: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

results.title: Pakistan minister to visit India, but no breakthrough expected
results.content: A Pakistani minister's visit to India for a Shanghai Cooperation Organization forum marks a rare high-level contact between the two archrivals, but analysts say it does not signal a resumption of bilateral engagement.

results.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya, top UN court rules
results.content: The International Court of Justice has upheld large parts of a genocide case against Myanmar linked to the 2017 conflict with its Rohingya minority. It called for it to pay reparations and let refugees return safely.

results.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
results.content: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

results.title: Almost 1 in 4 children live in conflict zones — report
results.content: Denial of humanitarian access, abductions and sexual violence are among several violations against children that have increased dramtically over the past year, according to a new report by Save the Children.

results.title: North Korea expanded uranium enrichment plant, says IAEA head
results.content: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi has said the ongoing expansion of North Korea's uranium enrichment program remains "a cause for serious concern."

results.title: India: Online censorship grows after 'Cockroach' protests
results.content: Since anti-government Cockroach protests erupted, journalists and creators say their content is increasingly being restricted on social media in India.

results.title: ICJ to rule on Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar: What to know
results.content: The ICJ is set to decide whether Myanmar's military operations in Rakhine State a decade ago were carried out with the intent to destroy the country's Rohingya minority, in whole or in part.
